i2_hydrocarbon_k_search: Wanted: primary measured K = [I2]hydrocarbon/[I2]water near 25 C (hexane, heptane or other alkane).

Found (primary, read): K1 = 80 for I2 between cyclohexane and 1.00 F H2SO4 at 25 C, Van de Steeg, Univ. New Mexico report/dissertation for the US AEC (1968), doi:10.2172/4770773, OSTI PDF p. 71 (K1 = [I2]nonaq/[I2]aq defined p. 70). Not hexane, not pure water; not adopted.

Not found as primary: any hexane/water or heptane/water I2 distribution coefficient. Secondary teaching pages give water/CCl4 = 0.0116-0.0117 (i.e. CCl4/water about 86), consistent with K = 85 being the classic CCl4 value, but Jakowkin (1895) itself was not reached.
